take a look at these PRs:

• *entireio/cli*: [#1945](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1945) — login: default to auth.entire.io and follow its regional handoff
• *entireio/auth-go*: [#20](https://github.com/entireio/auth-go/pull/20) — authcode, deviceflow: support region-dispatching authorization servers


rebase them on origin/main, and make sure they're still right.  we're about to deploy the entire-core side (the global auth.entire.io cli login handler), so i'll want to try out these branches.

also take a look at https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1945#discussion_r3755501377, see if it's worth addressing.

diff --git a/CHANGELOG.md b/CHANGELOG.md
index a1f2f03..029911d 100644
--- a/CHANGELOG.md
+++ b/CHANGELOG.md
@@ -2,6 +2,35 @@
 
 ## Unreleased
 
+### Added
+
+Support for authorization servers that are a *dispatching front door*: the
+apex serves `/authorize` and `/device_authorization` but redirects each to a
+regional authorization server, which is the only host that mints tokens and
+the only host that will redeem the resulting code. The client must therefore
+learn the region at runtime and send the token request there.
+
+- `authcode.Flow.Issuer()` — the RFC 9207 `iss` parameter from the loopback
+  callback, or `""` when the server sent none. Reported verbatim and
+  deliberately **not** validated: the package knows the origin it dialled but
+  not the issuer identifier the deployment expects, and for a dispatching
+  front door those legitimately differ (RFC 9207 §2.4 makes validation the
+  client's job). Callers MUST check it against their own trust policy.
+- `authcode.Flow.SetTokenBaseURL(baseURL)` — retargets this flow's token
+  exchange at `baseURL` instead of `Client.BaseURL`. Call it between `Wait`
+  and `Exchange`; `""` clears the override. `baseURL` is validated as an
+  origin (HTTPS unless `AllowInsecureHTTP` and loopback), but the package
+  cannot judge whether the host is trustworthy — the authorization code and
+  the user's tokens travel to it.
+- `deviceflow.DeviceCode.ResponseOrigin` — the origin that actually served
+  the device-authorization response, after any redirects the client followed.
+  Filled in by `StartDeviceAuth`, never decoded from the response body (that
+  body is parsed strictly, so a server-sent field of the same name would be a
+  breaking change). Equals `Client.BaseURL` when no redirect occurred.
+- `deviceflow.Client.TokenBaseURL` — overrides `BaseURL` for the token
+  endpoint only (`PollDeviceAuth` / `PollUntil`). Empty means "use BaseURL".
+  Set it between `StartDeviceAuth` and the first poll.
+
 ## v0.5.2 — 2026-07-07
 
 ### Added

458	// issMatches reports whether an issuer identifier is one this CLI accepts
459	// for a login dialled at expected. Both sides are stripped to a bare origin
460	// via api.OriginOnly first, so "https://issuer/" and "https://issuer" match.
461	// The caller has already rejected an empty iss claim.
462	//
463	// Two shapes are accepted:
464	//
465	//   - exact origin equality (the single-region case, and any dev/loopback
466	//     login server), and
467	//   - claimed is a strict subdomain of expected over https — the production
468	//     shape, where https://auth.entire.io is a dispatcher that hands the
469	//     login off to a regional login server such as
470	//     https://us.auth.entire.io, which is what actually mints the token.
471	//
472	// The subdomain rule is a delegation rule, not a string-prefix one:
473	// "auth.entire.io.evil.com" does not end in ".auth.entire.io", and a sibling
474	// like "entire.io" is not below it either. https is required so a
475	// dispatching host can never widen trust to a plaintext origin, and the port
476	// must match so ":443" and ":8443" stay distinct issuers.
477	func issMatches(claimed, expected string) error {
478		normClaimed := api.OriginOnly(claimed)
479		normExpected := api.OriginOnly(expected)
480		if normClaimed == normExpected {
481			return nil
482		}
483		if isDelegatedIssuer(normClaimed, normExpected) {
484			return nil
485		}
486		return fmt.Errorf("iss mismatch: token claims %q, expected %q or a subdomain of it", normClaimed, normExpected)
487	}
488	
489	// isDelegatedIssuer reports whether claimed is an https origin whose host
490	// sits strictly below expected's host, on the same port. Both arguments are
491	// already api.OriginOnly-normalised (lowercase, default port dropped, no
492	// path/query/fragment).
493	func isDelegatedIssuer(claimed, expected string) bool {
494		c, cErr := url.Parse(claimed)
495		e, eErr := url.Parse(expected)
496		if cErr != nil || eErr != nil {
497			return false
498		}
499		// https only, on both sides: a dispatcher reached over TLS must not be
500		// able to redirect the token exchange to a plaintext origin, and a
501		// plaintext (dev/loopback) login server gets no delegation at all.
502		if c.Scheme != schemeHTTPS || e.Scheme != schemeHTTPS {
503			return false
504		}
505		if c.Port() != e.Port() {
506			return false
507		}
508		claimedHost, expectedHost := c.Hostname(), e.Hostname()
509		if claimedHost == "" || expectedHost == "" {
510			return false
511		}
512		// The leading dot is what makes this a delegation check: it forces a
513		// label boundary, so neither "xauth.entire.io" nor "auth.entire.io.evil.com"
514		// qualifies under "auth.entire.io".
515		return strings.HasSuffix(claimedHost, "."+expectedHost)
516	}
517	
518	// adoptIssuer decides whether a login started against dialled may be
519	// completed at the issuer the login server named, and returns the origin the
520	// token request should go to ("" meaning "no change").
521	//
522	// This is the security-critical half of the dispatching-login-server
523	// support: the returned origin receives the authorization code (or the
524	// device code) and hands back the user's tokens, so it is gated by exactly
525	// the same rule as the iss claim on the token itself.
526	func adoptIssuer(claimed, dialled string) (string, error) {
527		normClaimed := api.OriginOnly(strings.TrimSpace(claimed))
528		if normClaimed == "" || normClaimed == api.OriginOnly(dialled) {
529			return "", nil
530		}
531		if err := issMatches(normClaimed, dialled); err != nil {
532			return "", fmt.Errorf("login server %s handed off to an unacceptable issuer: %w", api.OriginOnly(dialled), err)
533		}
534		return normClaimed, nil
535	}

+### `entire login`: the apex dispatches, a region issues
+
+`entire login --server` defaults to the apex `https://auth.entire.io`
+(`api.DefaultAuthBaseURL`). The apex is a **dispatcher, not an issuer**: it
+serves `/authorize` and `/device_authorization` and redirects each to the
+caller's regional core, and it serves no token endpoint, no discovery
+document, and no JWKS. Only a region mints tokens, with `iss`/`aud` set to

+token request there:
+

+  region, which appends the RFC 9207 `iss` parameter to the loopback
+  redirect. `runBrowserLogin` reads it (`BrowserAuthFlow.Issuer()`) and
+  redeems the code at that host (`UseTokenIssuer`). Posting the exchange to

+  reports the origin that actually answered, and `runLogin` points the token
+  poll at it.

Both branches are rebased, verified, and the Copilot nit is fixed. Nothing pushed.

**1. auth-go [#20](https://github.com/entireio/auth-go/pull/20) — no rebase needed.** `paul/regional-token-endpoint` (c43c075) already sits directly on `origin/main` (bb62b5d). `go test ./...` passes across all 9 packages. Latest tag is v0.5.2, so the CLI's `v0.5.3-0.20260811043916-c43c075b3c2a` pseudo-version is still correctly ordered.

**2. cli [#1945](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1945) — rebased clean over 97 commits.** No conflicts; `main` never touched `login.go`, `auth/`, or `api/base_url.go` in that window (only `api/trail_types.go` and unrelated README/Scoop docs). `mise run lint` = 0 issues, `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/{,auth/,api/}` pass, `go build ./...` resolves the auth-go pin.

**3. Copilot [r3755501377](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1945#discussion_r3755501377) — valid, fixed** in `47cfb2f97e`. `issMatches` unconditionally said *"expected X or a subdomain of it"*, but `isDelegatedIssuer` requires https on both sides, so against an http dev/loopback server the suggestion is a dead end. Now gated on a new `canDelegate`, with a table test (`login.go:486`, `login_issuer_test.go:74`).

**Correctness spot-checks that held up:**
- `persistLogin` still validates against the *dialled* host (`login.go:226,357`), so the regional `iss` goes through the subdomain rule rather than bypassing it — and `loginCompleteLine` prints the region.
- `adoptIssuer` can only ever return an **https** origin (exact-match returns `""`, delegation demands https both sides), so neither `UseTokenIssuer` path can be steered to plaintext even under `--insecure-http-auth`.
- Device-flow 307 replay works: `deviceflow` builds the POST with `strings.NewReader`, so `net/http` sets `GetBody` and re-sends the body; no `CheckRedirect` override.
- `DefaultAuthBaseURL` is referenced only by the `--server` default — the apex switch is scoped to login and can't leak into discovery/JWKS paths.
